title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

comments.body:
I reproduced this on Python 3.13 / Windows against `develop`, and I think I've found the cause.

**Root cause**

`AppTest._run()` builds a new `PagesManager` on every run, and its `_current_page_script_hash` starts out empty. `ScriptRunner` compares that against the requested page hash, sees a mismatch, and does the page-change cleanup. That cleanup drops page-persistent widget state. A browser session keeps one `PagesManager`, so it doesn't hit this, and `persist_state=session` isn't affected.

**Observed with the repro from the issue**

- Before: hidden state is `'SKU-42'`, but after showing the input again its value is `''`, with no exceptions.
- After the change below: hidden state is `'SKU-42'` and the shown value is `'SKU-42'`.

**Possible fix** in `lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py`, right after the `PagesManager` is constructed in `_run()`:

```python
pages_manager.set_current_page_script_hash(
    self._page_hash or pages_manager.main_script_hash
)
```

This marks the fresh manager as already on the current page. `switch_page()` still sets `self._page_hash`, so real page switches are still treated as page changes.

**Regression test** (`app_test_test.py`): toggle a `persist_state=page` text input, enter a value, hide it, show it again, and assert the value is preserved.

I ran the new test and the other AppTest tests, including the `switch_page` ones, and they pass. One existing test, `test_switch_page_uses_paths_relative_to_main_script`, fails on Windows with and without this change because of path escaping in its error-message assertion, so it is unrelated.

I know external PRs are paused, so I'm posting this as a diagnosis. I can share the patch if it's useful.

This is a bug in `AppTest`, reproduced on Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0: a keyed widget with `persist_state="page"` keeps its value while hidden, then comes back empty when shown again, even though the test never changes pages. A browser session keeps the value, and `persist_state="session"` keeps it in `AppTest`. `AppTest._run()` builds a new `PagesManager` on every run, and that manager's current page hash starts as `""`. `ScriptRunner` compares that empty hash with the target page (the main-script hash when no page was requested), treats the rerun as a page change, and runs page-change widget cleanup before `ScriptRunContext.reset()` installs the real page hash. Page-scoped persistence then sees a different page and drops the preserved value, including the pending reset that makes the remounted widget ignore its stored value. A contributor reproduced this on `develop`; seeding the new manager with the requested hash stops the false page change, but that also makes the current and requested hashes identical after `switch_page()`, so the pre-run cleanup that should drop page-scoped state before the new page registers widgets would be skipped. The seed needs to be the page from the previous run, with the requested hash passed separately.

### Related Issues

No duplicates found. These are nearby, with different failures:

- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) — `AppTest` can hit a session-state `KeyError` when conditional inputs disappear on rerun. Same test runner and dynamic widget tree; this issue drops a page-persistent value with no exception.
- [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) — `AppTest` raises `KeyError` when a rerun adds widgets and updates others. Same session-state tracking gap across reruns; the failure here is a silent reset of `persist_state="page"`.
- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) — Closed. A `persist_state=None` remount can reset the browser widget while `st.session_state` still holds the old value. Related persistence/remount bookkeeping, in the real runtime and for the default scope.

---
*This is an automated triage comment using `grok-4.7-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*

## Verification: confirmed

Reproduced on the reported 1.65.0 from PyPI and on `develop` (192c914271), macOS/arm64 with Python 3.12. The reported output matches verbatim, including the absence of `at.exception`.

| Environment | While hidden | After showing again |
|---|---|---|
| AppTest, streamlit 1.65.0 (PyPI) | `'SKU-42'` | `''` |
| AppTest, local `develop` @ 192c914271 | `'SKU-42'` | `''` |
| Real browser, same `develop` build | `'SKU-42'` | `'SKU-42'` |

The expectation in this report rests on a browser retaining the value, so I verified that directly rather than assuming it: running the same hide/show sequence in a browser against the same `develop` build keeps `SKU-42` in both the text input and `st.session_state`. The divergence is real — the browser is correct and AppTest is wrong.

Both controls behave as reported: `persist_state="session"` retains the value, and `persist_state=None` resets it (key absent while hidden).

### Mechanism

This agrees with the diagnosis already posted in this thread. `AppTest._run()` builds a fresh `PagesManager` and `LocalScriptRunner` on every `.run()` (`lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py:505`), so each run also gets a fresh `ScriptRunContext`. The page-change check at `lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py:660` compares `ctx.page_script_hash` against the resolved page hash and runs page-change widget cleanup on mismatch (`on_script_finished(widget_ids)`, line 694).

Instrumenting the five runs of the repro: `ctx.page_script_hash` is `''` on every run while the resolved hash is the stable main-script hash, so the page-change branch fires on 5/5 runs with zero page switches requested. Page-scoped persistence therefore sees a different page on each rerun and drops the value — which is exactly why the `"session"` control survives, since session scope ignores page changes. A browser session keeps one long-lived context, so the two hashes match and the branch never fires.

### Blast radius

The misclassification fires on every run, but its only observable consequence is `persist_state="page"` combined with an unmount/remount. Everything else I tested is unaffected:

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| Query params across reruns (this branch filters them) | survive |
| Plain keyed widget state, no `persist_state` | survives |
| `persist_state="page"` while the widget stays mounted | survives |
| `persist_state="page"` + unmount/remount | drops |

### Notes toward a fix

The one-line seed suggested above would also make the current and requested hashes identical after `switch_page()`, which skips the cleanup that *should* drop page-scoped state on a real page switch. The seed needs to be the page from the previous run, with the requested hash passed separately.

Separately, there is currently no AppTest coverage of `persist_state` anywhere under `lib/tests/streamlit/testing`, which is why this went unnoticed. Adding that coverage is cheap and catches the whole class; the harness page-model change is the part that needs care.

### Priority

Labeled `priority:P3`. AppTest-only with no production impact (browser behavior is correct), a narrow trigger, and a workaround available (`persist_state="session"` in the test, or asserting on `session_state` while the widget is mounted). Worth fixing, not urgent — would move up on additional user reports.
